title: Why Companies Won't Hire Junior Devs And Why It'll Backfire
description:
Why is the tech job market so hard right now, especially for new grads and junior developers? There's a deeper problem building underneath it.

Companies have stopped investing in junior devs — they only want senior engineers who are useful on day one. At the same time, breaches, hacks, and declining software quality are piling up, and senior engineers are retiring with nobody trained to replace them.

It's not a crisis yet, but it compounds: cut the pipeline of junior talent today, and in a few years there are no seniors left to fill the gap. The junior developer hiring freeze is quietly creating a future talent shortage.

#techwithtim #techjobs #softwareengineering #programming

top_comments.author: @daveofyorkshire301
top_comments.text:
Software isn't written anymore. It's a patchwork of already created libraries. Libraries that are common and therefore easy to analyze and find flaws and backdoors. 

Developers used to write a lot more, create unique solutions. Now they link up common code and create shrink-wrapped packages if they create anything. 

Coding is a list art, a costly and therefore restricted activity. Instead they find competent high level coders that can link up things to do what they want without any real understanding of how or what it's doing. 

So is it any wonder that finding issues, exploiting issues and attacking products becomes easier when they are utilizing a well known and easily available functional library to make everything look and feel the same.
